payload.detail: CORRECTED 2026-09-20/21 by measurement; the cause remains an inference. WHAT IS MEASURED: the claim that the workflow 'fails on every PR' is FALSE as stated. Runs 11, 12, 15, 17, 18, 20, 23, 24 and 25 of claude-review.yml all concluded SUCCESS between 14:58 and 16:04 on 2026-09-20; it then failed on PR #2900 twice (runs 29 att1/att2) and on PR #2939 (run 30) inside a five-minute window at 16:15-16:20, and failed again on PR #2966 at 08:10 on 2026-09-21. The 2026-09-20 failures were identical: duration_ms ~1900, num_turns 1, total_cost_usd 0, permission_denials_count 0, modelUsage {} - the run died on its first request having read no file, on two different branches with two different diffs, minutes apart. WHAT THAT ESTABLISHES: the failure is account-level. It is not a property of any diff and not a defect in the workflow definition. WHAT IT DOES NOT ESTABLISH: which account-level cause. A usage or concurrency limit on the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN subscription is the LEADING HYPOTHESIS, because this workflow exists to escape exactly that failure mode in three other reviewers (CodeRabbit categorical, Codex usage limits, Bugbot spend cap - all three recorded in the workflow header, and Bugbot posted 'usage limit reached' again on #2900 at 17:24). But token expiry or revocation, a transient provider outage and other account-level faults are NOT ruled out by this evidence, and the 2026-09-21 failure arrived after a long idle gap on the first review of the day, which fits a pure concurrency story poorly. Treat the cause as unconfirmed. SECOND CORRECTION: the check is red but ADVISORY. The row's 'paints a red check' is literally true - the job conclusion is failure and GitHub renders it red - but its implication that this gates a merge is false. .github/workflows/claude-review.yml sets continue-on-error: true at job level and the workflow is absent from pr-required's needs, so the RUN concludes success while the JOB shows failure, and the red cannot block a merge. The workflow header states this deliberately. ALSO WORTH KNOWING: 'synchronize' is not one of its triggers (only opened and ready_for_review), so a PR that takes further pushes after its one review never gets re-reviewed, and the red job conclusion stays pinned to a stale head where a reader will mistake it for current. NEXT ACTION for whoever picks this up: capture and surface the provider error the action currently swallows, because without it the cause cannot be settled; then decide whether a zero-usage first-request failure should be retried with backoff rather than surfaced.
payload.source: Session 2026-09-20/21, PRs #2900 and #2966; claude-review.yml run history 11-30 and job logs 106107924930, 106108413981 and 106259217832
payload.summary: Automated Claude review intermittently dies on its first request with zero usage, leaving a red advisory check that cannot block a merge
